title: Airwall deployment requirements - Lighthouse Labs
customer_attendees: Dr. Priya Narang (Head of AI Ops)
summary: Initial scoping for a physically isolated (airwall) on-prem Redwood deployment. Covered hardware footprint, signed-update process, internal audit needs, KMS/HSM integration, and timeline for a pilot. Customers want deterministic latency and an offline patch workflow; ask for security pack and HW worksheet.
action_items: Maya Chen: send Private deployment security pack and SOC2 summary - due 2025-07-11
Tomas Rivera: prepare HW footprint worksheet and reference quantization profiles - due 2025-07-14
Ethan Cole: share rack floor plan and existing switch model list - due 2025-07-10
next_steps: Redwood to share signed-update flow doc and sample firmware signing key process
Schedule a 2-hour technical deep dive with on-site infra team (TBD week of 7/21)
Customer to run initial capacity spreadsheet and return with expected qps/seq lengths
transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2025-07-08, Start: 15:00 UTC, Duration: 48 minutes. Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Tomas (Redwood SE), Janelle (CSM), Priya, Ethan, Marco, Leah.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time — I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on the account. um quick roll call?
[00:12] Priya: hi this is Priya, Head of AI Ops at Lighthouse Labs, thanks.
[00:15] Ethan: Ethan here, IT Ops.
[00:18] Marco: Marco, infrastructure.
[00:20] Leah: Leah, regulatory.
[00:23] Tomas: Tomas, solutions engineer at Redwood. Janelle: Janelle, customer success.
[00:30] Maya: goal today is to understand your isolation requirements, offline update cadence, and hardware constraints so we can recommend Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private with an airwall option. please tell us the must-haves.
[00:45] Priya: sure. high level — we need the inference system to sit in a physically isolated rack in our secured data center. no egress to the internet except an explicit jump box that gets audited. we call it an airwall. patching has to be scheduled windows and signed by our security team before applying, and we need full audit logs retained for two years.
[01:12] Ethan: also latency is important for our clinician-facing UI, we want tail latency below 180ms for short prompts (<=256 tokens). bulk batch jobs can be off-peak.
[01:26] Tomas: ok that's helpful. when you say "signed", do you have a signing key management process in place today? HSM or K M S? (note: transcript captured as K M S sometimes)
[01:38] Leah: we use an on-prem HSM, Thales. keys are guarded and rotated every quarter. no external key escrow allowed.
[01:46] Maya: great — Redwood Private supports integrating with customer KMS/HSMs; we usually do a local KMS adapter with our control plane disabled by default in airwall mode. Tomas, can you explain high level signed-update flow?
[02:05] Tomas: yeah. so for airwall deployments we ship artifacts as signed packages. customer pulls packages into a jump-box (which is inside their DMZ) after verifying sigs with their HSM, then pushes to the isolated rack. updates are staged in a canary subset of nodes if they want — though in some fully isolated setups customers run a manual canary. note: our runtime validates kernel signatures and model manifests before loading.
[02:36] Marco: how do you handle model KV cache and checkpointing? our workflows need resuming long-running sessions. sometimes transcripts read as 'kay-v cache' — not sure exactly.
[02:48] Tomas: right. Redwood uses a distributed KV cache to keep per-request state; in Private we persist the KV on local NVMe with encrypted disks. For long sessions we recommend pinning a model snapshot and enabling periodic checkpointing to a secure NFS inside the airwall. That avoids any egress.
[03:12] Priya: ok, and hardware — do you have recommendations for GPUs per rack? we currently have a mix of A100s and a couple of older T4s.
[03:24] Tomas: we usually match model families to GPU class. for high-throughput short-latency chat loads, 8xA100 (80GB) per rack is common baseline. if you're running quantized 4-bit variants you can fit more instances on a single GPU. we'll send a hw worksheet so we can map QPS to GPU hours.
[03:46] Ethan: what about air-gapped monitoring? we still need metrics and traces but prefer the data stay internal.
[03:55] Janelle: Redwood Console for Private can be deployed inside the airwall — no telemetry leaves unless you enable it. logs and metrics are stored on customer provided storage and we provide dashboards. we also do an ops agent that can push alert webhooks to your internal pager.
[04:12] Leah: the auditors will ask about privileged access and SSO. what SAML/S S O patterns do you support?
[04:20] Maya: we support SAML 2.0 and OIDC, and RBAC via LDAP/AD integration. for private, admin control plane is optional — you can run a read-only control plane outside and a full control plane inside.
[04:33] Marco: is there an automatic fallback if a node crashes? we can't have long downtime during clinic hours.
[04:40] Tomas: yes, we surface failover policies — for single-rack you'd want redundant instances with automatic requeueing. for tough SLOs customers often do a two-rack active-passive setup. note: exactly how long new node cold-starts depends on model size due to KV warmup.
[04:59] Priya: hmm, what's your cold start for a 30B model roughly?
[05:04] Tomas: depends on quant and kernel optimizations — with continuous batching and prewarm we aim for 10-20s cold start on 80GB A100 for a 30B that isn't pinned. if you pre-pin the model in memory and keep the KV warm it's sub-second for requests.
[05:21] Ethan: you mentioned KV and prewarm — does that increase cost materially?
[05:26] Tomas: yes, there's a memory and GPU-lifecycle cost. pre-pinning consumes GPU resident memory and prevents that slot from serving other models, so it's a tradeoff between cost and guaranteed latency. Redwood Optimize can model that tradeoff for your workload.
[05:42] Priya: our security team will insist on signed firmware for the nodes themselves, not just packages. do you work with signed BIOS/Firmware?
[05:51] Maya: Redwood doesn't manage firmware, that's typically handled by your datacenter/ops. we document supported server models and firmware versions. for strict compliance customers we coordinate a signed firmware checklist but don't hold the signing keys.
[06:06] Leah: audit trail — we need tamper-evident logs for 24 months with append-only storage. can you support that?
[06:15] Janelle: yes, we support immutable log write-once S3-compatible stores or a local WORM solution; our audit logs include request metadata and model version hashes.
[06:28] Priya: ok great. timeline — we want a pilot in Q3, ideally a 6-week pilot. what does Redwood need to start?
[06:36] Maya: primary things: rack floor plan, expected queries per second per endpoint, sample prompt distributions (seq lengths), and your HSM integration docs. we'll need a signed NDA for on-site pre-audit if you want us physically in the facility.
[06:53] Ethan: about costs — if we go private airwall with dedicated rack, how do you price? flat monthly for reserved capacity?
[07:01] Maya: for Dedicated/Private we do a reserved capacity contract — monthly, with a hardware advisory, plus an installation and support fee. exact numbers depend on GPU count and support tier. we'll put a rough estimate in the security pack.
[07:15] Marco: security nuance — if we can't allow external control plane, how do we get patches and critical security alerts?
[07:23] Tomas: two options: 1) push model and runtime packages to your jump-box after you fetch from our staging (pull model), or 2) use an air-gapped USB/signed media process. Critical CVEs can be delivered via signed packages and a manual apply workflow. we also support an email/SMS out-of-band alert channel for ops staff.
[07:46] Priya: what's the rollback story if an update misbehaves in the isolated rack?
[07:52] Tomas: every update includes a model manifest and rollback tag. by default we keep last known-good snapshots and you can trigger a rollback which redeploys the previous package and rehydrates KV from a checkpoint. we recommend snapshotting before any major update.
[08:07] Leah: will we be able to run pen tests against the deployment? our compliance team requires regular tests.
[08:13] Maya: yes, customers can run pentests; we provide a pentest-ready checklist and a review window so the test doesn't impair operations. results can be shared under NDA.
[08:25] Ethan: do you support disconnected telemetry ingestion? for example, we might periodically ship metrics via encrypted tapes or a secure jump box export.
[08:36] Tomas: we support scheduled metric export to an internal metrics store, and a bulk export tool that can write batched metrics to a tarball for offline transfer. it's not as granular as live telemetry but acceptable for airwalled environments.
[08:50] Priya: one more — model provenance. we need to know model lineage, who touched weights, when introduced. does Redwood provide immutable model manifests?
[08:59] Tomas: yes, every model version has a manifest with git hash, training metadata (if provided), and a signing chain. manifests are signed and included in the package so you can verify provenance offline.
[09:15] Marco: question on RBAC and least privilege — can we limit runtime to only accept requests from a specific internal subnet and restrict which service accounts can call certain models?
[09:25] Tomas: yes, network-level ACLs plus token-level RBAC. tokens are issued by your AD/SAML provider and mapped to roles in the runtime.
[09:33] Priya: ok good. other risks — supply chain for kernel libs. auditors ask about third-party libs and CVE scanning.
[09:42] Janelle: we publish SBOMs for runtime components and can provide a CVE scan report for the release you will deploy.
[09:51] Ethan: any limitations around model size? we sometimes want to run a bespoke 70B model that isn't in the Redwood catalog.
[09:58] Tomas: Private supports any model you can fit on the GPU, but larger models increase cold-start and footprint. we also support loading off-card attention optimizations but performance varies. we'll run an expected SLO analysis once you share model size and profile.
[10:15] Priya: can Redwood help with quantization tooling? we have internal ML folks but limited infra to test 4-bit runs.
[10:22] Tomas: yes, Redwood Optimize includes quantization suggestions, and we can provide reference workflows and scripts for 4-bit/PTQ quantization we used for similar customers. we can do a short engagement to help tune it.
[10:35] Maya: wrapping up — to be concrete, we'll send: security pack, sample signed-update process doc, HW worksheet, and SOC2 summary. Tomas will follow up with quant and model footprint notes. we'll schedule the deep-dive after we get your rack details.
[10:50] Priya: perfect. one last ask — can you include a sample runbook for incident response in the audit pack?
[10:57] Maya: yes, we'll include a runbook template that you can customize.
[11:03] Ethan: thanks all.
[11:05] Maya: thanks everyone. next steps recap in chat and we'll email the docs.

End of transcript.
